groups.label: Position of a point relative to a circle

statements.text: If A is outside the circle, then MA > r, and vice versa.
If A is on the circle, then MA = r, and vice versa.
If A is inside the circle, then MA < r, and vice versa.

context.text: In the figure opposite, circle M divides the points of the plane in to three sets of points.

Imagine a Wi-Fi router at point $M$ that reaches phones up to $15$ m away, so its range is a circle of radius $r = 15$ m. A phone at point $A$ is $MA = 2x - 3$ metres from the router. For which values of $x$ is the phone outside the router's range?

statements.text: The straight line L is located outside the circle M, L ∩ circle M = ϕ; so MA > r and vice versa. Formula: $L \cap M = \phi, \ MA > r$
The straight line L is a secant to the circle M, L ∩ circle M = {C, D}; so MA < r and vice versa. Formula: $L \cap M = \{C, D\}, \ MA < r$
The straight line L is tangent to circle M, L ∩ the circle = {A}; so MA = r and vice versa. Formula: $L \cap M = \{A\}, \ MA = r$
A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at its point of tangency.
If a straight line is perpendicular to a diameter of a circle at one of its endpoints, then it is a tangent to the circle.

context.text: Suppose a circular fountain has centre $M$ and radius $5$ m. Three straight paths run past it, and the shortest distance from $M$ to each path is $3$ m, $5$ m and $7$ m. Which path misses the fountain, which cuts across it, and which just touches it at one point?

statements.text: The straight line l = line MN is called the line of centers of the two circles M and N, and it is an axis of symmetry for both of them.
Point 4: If $MN = r_1 - r_2$, then $M \cap N = \ldots$ (blank), surface of circle M ∩ surface of circle N = ... (blank), and the two circles are touching internally.
Point 5: If $MN < r_1 - r_2$, then $M \cap N = \ldots$ (blank), surface of circle M ∩ surface of circle N = ... (blank), and the two circles are intersecting as in figure ... (blank).
When $MN = 0$ (zero), the two circles are concentric, as in figure ... (blank).

context.text: Imagine two routers at points $M$ and $N$ whose ranges are circles of radii $9$ m and $4$ m. They are placed $MN = 5$ m apart. How do the two range circles sit relative to each other: separate, touching, overlapping or one inside the other?

statements.text: The line of centers of two touching circles passes through a point of tangency and is perpendicular to the common tangent.
The line of centers of two intersecting circles is perpendicular to the common chord and bisects it.
If ABC is a right-angled triangle at A and AD ⊥ BC, then (AB)² = BD × BC (Euclidean theorem). Formula: $(AB)^2 = BD \times BC$
Also (AD)² = DB × DC (Corollary). Formula: $(AD)^2 = DB \times DC$
Also AD × BC = AB × AC. Formula: $AD \times BC = AB \times AC$

context.text: Suppose two garden sprinklers at $M$ and $N$ each water a circle of radius $5$ m, and the centres are $MN = 6$ m apart. The two circles cross at points $A$ and $B$. How long is the straight line $AB$ between those two crossing points?
